values: Movement cost by axis and tile crossing
Both directions pooled. Camera crossings and delayed back-table updates are distinct events.
FPS = clock / mean presentation interval. This does not imply stable cadence or a causal phase-only comparison.
Movement follows real keyboard input. Every moving sample is unclamped and its displacement matches elapsed VBlanks.
Selected disjoint child routines, inclusive cycles/frame. Their sum is not the complete rendering cost.
Idle includes released-key settling samples and outliers while alternate back tables settle.
Fine phase zero is not equivalent to a crossing: reverse movement can cross from phase 0 to 7.
Cycles per call include guest timing and waits. Never sum inclusive parents and children.
P95 = nearest-rank 95th percentile. ISR entry/vector latency is charged to its interrupted context.
Self = inclusive minus tracked child spans; untracked helpers remain in their nearest measured owner.
Software frames 5..484; warmed start. Negative margin exceeds the proposed single-60-Hz draw interval.
Clock and scanline model: scripts/msx/inputs.py; ROM selects R9=$82 (50 Hz).
262 × 228 cycles is the proposed 60 Hz comparison; no 60 Hz gameplay validation yet.
Interpretation of the user budget: 5,000 cycles; actual usable VBlank deadline remains to be measured.
isolated horizontal/vertical routes, both directions, normal/Shift and idle
Contributor ROM; no graphics or original ROM bytes are embedded in this workbook.
Measured using emulated time × clock, not host wall time or opcode-table estimates.
clock_irq measures ISR body through RETI; hardware entry and vector jump are excluded from its row.
calls.tsv records every call; frames.tsv and control-frames.tsv retain independent frame observations.
profile.py asserts nested-cost reconciliation, complete routine coverage and control-run agreement.
Performance priority: approach 30 FPS with measured worst-case margins.
User has final acceptance of every graphical or perceptual concession.
SCREEN 4, right-edge simplification and fixed 8-pixel left mask are approved only for this laboratory.
Flag pauses are scheduling candidates; define event duration, bounded work and resume behavior.
No physical hardware test; production AI, sound and flag capture are outside this workload.
